page: Microsoft Azure F8ads_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor capable of clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 8 dedicated physical x86_64 cores operating with a single thread per core, avoiding resource contention typical of hyper-threaded architectures. It comes equipped with 32.0 GB of system RAM, offering 4.0 GB per vCPU, and bundles 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the platform supports vector computing extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-threaded capabilities. In single-core stress-ng tests, the F8ads_v7 places in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, matched by top-tier single-threaded compression throughput in gzip and bzip3 routines. The processor also achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M parameter language models. Across multi-core stress-ng, PassMark CPU suites, and medium-scale model inference, the instance sits within the middle 50 percent, delivering linear multi-threaded scaling consistent with an 8-core physical allocation.

The bundling of dedicated physical cores and integrated NVMe scratch storage yields high architectural efficiency for IOPS-sensitive and single-thread bound operations without requiring external disk attachments. However, with no discrete GPU accelerator and a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, it is not structured for memory-intensive data mining or large model training. The instance is best suited for CI/CD build environments, batch data compression, web serving, and database applications requiring rapid local storage access and high clock rates.
description: Microsoft Azure F8ads_v7 is an AMD-powered compute virtual machine featuring an 8-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading. The platform integrates 32.0 GB of memory and 944 GB of local NVMe SSD storage under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, supporting extended instructions like AVX-512. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU throughput and data compression performance, alongside mid-range multi-core compute and memory metrics. While lacking discrete GPU acceleration and constrained by moderate memory density, the combination of dedicated execution threads and fast local NVMe storage delivers strong performance efficiency for single-thread critical and disk-intensive tasks. Best-fit workloads include CI/CD pipelines, compilation tasks, web application hosting, and local relational or key-value databases.
